happens: a jammed window comes loose when you push hard with both hands
point: Real effort with your whole weight frees what was stuck.
natural: no - you push the window or sash, not 'lean into the frame'; the frame is the fixed part

happens: you reply in a foreign language without translating in your head
point: Long practice has made the skill automatic.
natural: yes
known: no - only people who have learned a second language to a working level

happens: after days of solo practice a first full sentence comes out
point: A first small success after private practice.
natural: no - unclear what is being practised (a language? a speech? speaking again?) and 'comes out whole' is vague
known: no - too unspecific to recognise; depends on guessing the situation

happens: another person remembers how you like your coffee
point: Being noticed and remembered in a small way.
natural: yes

happens: you refuse credit and name the person who really did the work
point: Honesty about who deserves the credit.
natural: yes

actor: you, writing a message on a phone
happens: you type a reply in a rush and then hesitate before sending
point: Pausing before sending something written in the heat of the moment.
natural: yes

happens: small monthly savings have added up to the price of a course
point: Small regular savings quietly add up to something real.
natural: no - 'have become the course fee' is slightly odd; savings cover or add up to a fee

actor: you and an earlier writer of the recipe
happens: you have added one change of your own to someone else's handwritten recipe
point: Something inherited, with your own small mark added.
natural: no - 'in another hand' for handwriting is old-fashioned and may be misread
known: no - handwritten recipe cards are uncommon now

happens: a song plays during the dishes and two people sing along
point: An ordinary chore turns into a shared happy moment.
natural: no - people 'join in', voices don't 'join it'; mildly awkward

happens: you wait and let a child keep trying to do up a zip
point: Patience: letting someone learn by doing it themselves.
natural: yes

happens: you hold back what you want to say until the other person finishes
point: Restraint: not interrupting.
natural: no - 'the other' is stiff; 'the other person' is normal

happens: wind flips an umbrella inside out, it is pushed back into shape
point: Something knocked out of shape is righted and carries on.
natural: no - 'and goes on' is unclear: an umbrella doesn't go on; the person is missing from the sentence

happens: the same table has been kept through three house moves
point: A lasting object that stays constant through change.
natural: no - 'moved through three homes' is slightly off; and 'still stands in the kitchen' of which home is blurred

actor: rain and a group of people
happens: rain cancels an outdoor plan and everyone gathers in the kitchen
point: A spoiled plan turns into a warm gathering.
natural: yes

happens: a child ties a lace badly and you do not step in
point: Holding back from fixing someone else's mistake.
natural: yes

actor: you, about to post a photo
happens: you notice someone in the photo who did not consent to it being posted
point: A moment of conscience about another person's privacy.
natural: no - 'a face that was never asked' is odd; you ask a person, not a face

happens: wind flattens the grass and it stands up again later
point: Bending under pressure and recovering.
natural: yes
known: no - most people don't watch a field through the day; it is nature imagery, not lived experience

happens: you thread a needle automatically the way you were once taught
point: An old learned skill stays in the hands.
natural: yes

actor: a lopsided cake and the guests
happens: a cake comes out leaning and everyone asks for a slice from the lower side
point: Unclear - maybe the flaw is what people like.
plausible: no - there is no real reason everyone would want the low end; it reads as invented
natural: no - 'the low end' of a cake is odd, and the point of the sentence is unclear
known: no - a lopsided cake yes, but not this reaction

happens: a seedling wilts after repotting and then grows a new leaf
point: Recovery after a setback; slow adjustment to a new place.
natural: yes
known: no - only people who grow plants would recognise it

happens: someone says the unspoken thing and the atmosphere changes
point: Speaking a truth aloud changes everything.
natural: yes

happens: a runner drops to a walk on a hill but keeps going
point: Slowing down without giving up.
natural: yes

happens: you rotate the map and suddenly understand where you are
point: A small adjustment makes things make sense.
natural: yes

happens: a flight is cancelled at the last minute and plans must be redone
point: A sudden disruption forces a full replan.
natural: no - 'the day has to be made again' is not idiomatic; a day is replanned or rearranged

happens: two people walk together at a pace neither consciously set
point: Easy, unspoken harmony between two people.
natural: no - 'Two walk' with no noun is stiff

happens: a plan sounds different once you say it out loud
point: Speaking a plan aloud tests it.
natural: yes

happens: a parcel is delivered with no indication who sent it
point: A small mystery; something unexpected and unexplained.
natural: yes
known: no - it happens, but rarely; most parcels are expected and labelled

happens: a message reads differently when you look at it again the next morning
point: Mood changes how words are read.
natural: yes

happens: the electricity fails, cutting off a video call and losing unsaved work
point: Sudden loss of work through something outside your control.
plausible: no - most people work on battery laptops with autosave, so a power cut drops the call but rarely loses the slide
natural: yes
known: no - losing unsaved work yes, but this exact combination is uncommon today

happens: two people manoeuvre a long mirror through a door, taking turns to move
point: Careful cooperation; one waits while the other moves.
natural: yes

happens: one sentence in a voice message changes how the day feels
point: A few words can change the whole day.
natural: yes

actor: you and an old voice recording
happens: you find a recording you made and don't remember its content
point: Something of your own you have forgotten.
natural: no - 'a recording in your own voice' is awkward; 'of your own voice' is normal
known: no - only people who record voice memos have had this

happens: a street that seemed unfamiliar at night turns out to be a known one at dawn
point: Daylight shows the familiar behind what looked strange.
natural: no - the tenses and 'the one you know' take a second reading to untangle

happens: a phone falls on a tiled floor and the breakage takes over the evening
point: One small accident hijacks everything.
natural: yes

actor: two people with a two-handed saw
happens: the saw cuts well when the two take turns pulling
point: Work goes smoothly when two people alternate in rhythm.
natural: no - verbless first half; 'a long saw' is not the usual name (two-man or crosscut saw)
known: no - almost nobody today has used a two-person saw

happens: people have worn a path across grass where no path was planned
point: Real habits override the official design.
natural: no - 'is on no plan' is stiff

happens: you are told a result is available but not what it says
point: The suspense of waiting to learn an important result.
natural: no - 'and nothing yet about what it is' is clumsy

happens: you have opened a new document and not yet written anything
point: A fresh start; everything is still open.
natural: yes

happens: with the battery almost gone you send only the essential message
point: Scarcity forces you to pick what really matters.
natural: yes

happens: a friend uses your habitual phrase and you hear it from outside
point: Seeing yourself reflected in someone else.
natural: no - 'come out of a friend's mouth' is slightly crude and 'learn how it sounds' is vague

happens: you drive past your turn-off because you were on autopilot
point: Ease makes you inattentive.
natural: no - 'because the road was so easy to follow' is an odd reason as worded; 'turning' is British only

happens: someone opens the door a crack on the chain to check the visitor
point: Caution: checking before letting someone in.
natural: yes
known: no - door chains are no longer common; many know it only from films

happens: you skip a box on a form because it has no label
point: Leaving alone what you can't identify.
plausible: no - forms with a completely unlabelled box are rare
natural: yes
known: no - confusing forms yes, an unlabelled box hardly ever

happens: you see that someone else needs the last free seat more than you
point: Recognising another person's greater need at once.
natural: yes

happens: a friend describes an evening and their version of you surprises you
point: Others see you differently from how you see yourself.
natural: no - 'as someone you had not met' is clever but takes a moment to parse

happens: after a few lengths the swimming becomes rhythmic and automatic
point: Settling into an effortless rhythm.
natural: no - swimming is never named; 'lengths' and 'strokes' must be decoded
known: no - only people who swim lengths

happens: you pick up an unknown call and withhold your name until the caller identifies themselves
point: Guardedness with strangers.
natural: yes

actor: a bare wall / the new tenant
happens: one wall in a new flat is still empty and undecided
point: An open space still waiting for a decision.
natural: no - 'nothing has been decided for it' is slightly stiff

happens: the water supply is off and one bottle must cover every need
point: Making do with very little.
natural: yes
known: no - water cut-offs are occasional; many adults have rarely had one

happens: a friend imitates your foot-tapping, a habit you were unaware of
point: Others notice habits you can't see in yourself.
plausible: no - friends rarely mimic a foot-tap; the scene feels constructed
natural: no - 'and you had never noticed it' is ambiguous (the copying or the tapping?)
known: no - being told about a habit yes, this scene no

happens: looking for a dropped key you also find a long-lost earring
point: Searching for one thing turns up another you had given up.
natural: yes

happens: the phone is put on silent overnight except for three chosen contacts
point: Shutting the world out but staying reachable for a few.
natural: yes

happens: a candle saved for a special occasion has never been used
point: Saving things for a 'right moment' that never comes.
natural: yes

happens: a waterfall has frozen solid against the rock
point: Movement stopped and held in place by cold.
natural: no - 'its last streams held against the rock' is poetic and vague
known: no - few adults have ever seen a frozen waterfall

happens: you brake by reflex when the car in front starts to wander
point: The body reacts before the mind understands.
natural: no - 'before you know why' is tacked on at the end and at first attaches to the drifting car

happens: a brighter new bulb reveals an old crack in the ceiling
point: Better light shows what was always there.
natural: yes

happens: the fog clears and the marker the walker was aiming for comes into view
point: You were on course all along without seeing it.
natural: no - 'the marker' is vague (what kind?) and 'is there' is flat and unclear
known: no - only hill or trail walkers

happens: a rarely used battery turns out to be dead when it is finally needed
point: Neglected things fail you exactly when needed.
natural: no - 'the battery you never use' is vague; which battery?

happens: bubbles rise through the water and are trapped under the ice
point: Something rising is stopped by an invisible barrier.
natural: no - 'then stops' for a chain of bubbles is odd; dark water but clear ice is hard to picture
known: no - very few people have watched this

happens: you speak more quietly when your friend falls silent, without knowing why
point: Sensing another's mood before understanding it.
natural: yes

happens: an idea strikes while walking and you stop to hold on to it
point: Catching a fleeting idea before it is lost.
natural: yes

happens: the cloud clears and you see how high you have already climbed
point: You have come further than you realised.
natural: no - 'the cloud opens' is unusual; clouds part or lift
known: no - only people who walk in mountains

happens: a bicycle left in the shed gets a rusty chain
point: What isn't used decays.
natural: yes

actor: a water drop on an icicle
happens: a drop freezes at the icicle's tip instead of dripping off
point: A moment caught and frozen just before it would have happened.
natural: no - 'has frozen ... just before it falls' contradicts itself: a frozen drop does not fall; should be 'before it could fall'
known: no - people know icicles but have not watched a drop freeze

happens: you turn back at the door feeling you've forgotten something unidentified
point: A nagging sense of something forgotten.
natural: no - 'sure something is left' is clipped; 'left behind' is what is meant

happens: you bring food to a shared meal and take home someone else's
point: Give and take; sharing comes back to you.
natural: yes

actor: daylight / you who chose a colour
happens: daylight shows the colour you picked under a lamp looks different
point: Things chosen in one light look different in another.
natural: no - 'is another colour' is abrupt and it is unclear what was coloured (paint? fabric?)

happens: a tight lid resists and finally opens with a full grip
point: Persistence and full effort finally work.
natural: no - 'when your whole hand closes on it' is odd; a lid needs grip and twist, and jar is never named

happens: the lift gets stuck between floors while the building carries on as normal
point: Being stuck while everything else goes on.
natural: no - 'the building goes on humming around it' is fanciful
known: no - most adults have never been stuck in a lift

happens: dough left covered overnight rises to twice its size
point: Things grow on their own if left to rest.
natural: yes
known: no - only people who bake with yeast

happens: someone silently halves the last piece to share it
point: Unspoken fairness and consideration.
natural: yes

happens: everyone agreed informally but only you put your name on the form
point: Others agree in private; you alone carry the responsibility.
natural: no - it is unclear what form or what was agreed; needs working out

happens: an exhausted person still gets up the final flight of stairs
point: Finding strength when you thought there was none.
natural: no - present 'is climbed' with past 'had nothing left' jars, and the passive is stiff

actor: a tree grown from a sapling
happens: a tree planted years ago has grown big enough to shade the bench
point: Something planted long ago now gives back.
natural: no - 'the sapling ... now shades' is illogical; it is no longer a sapling
known: no - few people have planted a tree and sat under it years later

happens: a broken bone heals unseen inside a plaster cast
point: Healing happens invisibly.
natural: no - 'nothing can be seen of it' is ambiguous (the bone, the break, or the healing?)

happens: one fetches the coffee while the other has kept a seat, with no scorekeeping
point: Easy mutual give-and-take without keeping score.
natural: no - tense shifts ('brings' / 'has saved') and 'One ... the other' with no nouns is stiff

actor: you, a player in a match
happens: you honestly report the ball was out and it costs your team the point
point: Honesty at your own cost.
plausible: no - in refereed sport players almost never volunteer calls against their own side
natural: yes
known: no - only people who play team sports, and even they rarely do this
